title: Jaismine Lamboria's Journey From Hospital Bed to Commonwealth Games Gold in Glasgow
excerpt: The Indian boxer and reigning world champion overcame a 14-day hospitalization and just three weeks of training to defeat Northern Ireland's Michaela Walsh 5-0 for CWG gold in the women's 57kg.
body:
• Jaismine Lamboria won the women's 57kg boxing gold at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, defeating defending champion Michaela Walsh of Northern Ireland by a unanimous 5-0 decision
  • Just weeks before the Games, Lamboria was hospitalized for 14 days in Mohali with a bacterial infection and resumed training only on July 1 — giving her barely three weeks to prepare
  • The Bhiwani-born boxer, who is the reigning world champion and world No. 1, upgraded her Birmingham 2022 bronze to gold while also serving as a Naib Subedar in the Indian Army

From Fever to the Final

Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria was not thinking about medals. She was searching for answers about a recurring fever that would not go away.

Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual, and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali, where doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection and put her on an intensive 14-day course of medication, according to The Times of India.

"I was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didn't know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days," Lamboria told The Times of India.

A Three-Week Sprint to Glasgow

When she was discharged, barely three weeks remained before the Commonwealth Games. Lamboria started training only on July 1, beginning with warm-ups, walking, and stretching before gradually ramping up intensity.

"I started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient," she said.

The physical recovery was only part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness did not break Lamboria's confidence.

"When I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda ma'am. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down."

— Jaismine Lamboria, 2026 CWG gold medalist

A Commanding Final

That resilience was on full display in Glasgow. In the women's 57kg final on August 1, Lamboria faced Northern Ireland's Michaela Walsh, the defending Commonwealth Games champion. The bout started cautiously, with the referee intervening twice in the opening minute to encourage engagement. Lamboria edged the first round 3-2 with cleaner punches, according to ESPN.

In the second round, Walsh tried to draw Lamboria into attacking, but the Indian remained patient, picking her shots with precision. The judges awarded her the round 5-0. In the final round, Walsh needed a big finish but Lamboria never let the defending champion gain momentum, sealing the round 4-1 for a comprehensive 5-0 unanimous decision victory, as reported by ANI.

A Boxing Legacy Runs Deep

Lamboria, born on August 30, 2001, in Bhiwani, Haryana, carries boxing in her blood. Her late great-grandfather Hawa Singh won gold medals in the heavyweight category at the 1966 and 1970 Asian Games. Her grandfather Chander Bhan Lamboriya was a wrestler, and her uncles Sandeep Singh and Parvinder Singh — both boxers — gave her initial training, according to Wikipedia.

In 2022, she became the first woman boxer to join the Indian Army, enlisting as a havildar in the Corps of Military Police. She has since been promoted to Naib Subedar. Her career resume includes a bronze at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, representation at the 2024 Paris Olympics, and gold medals at both the 2025 World Boxing Cup and the 2025 World Boxing Championships in Liverpool.

India's Boxing Dominance in Glasgow

Lamboria's gold was part of a historic boxing campaign by India at Glasgow 2026. Indian boxers won seven gold medals and three silvers across the boxing events, with Preeti Pawar (54kg), Sakshi Choudhary (51kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Arundhati Chaudhary (70kg), Sachin Siwach (60kg), and Ankush Panghal (80kg) all clinching gold, according to ESPN.

Her father, Jaiveer, celebrated from Bhiwani: "We are very happy that my daughter has made the entire nation proud. She will win a gold medal for the nation in the Olympics also," he told ANI.

What's Next

With the world championship title and Commonwealth gold now in her collection, Lamboria's next target is likely the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. At 24, the world No. 1 has time on her side — and as Glasgow proved, the resilience to overcome whatever obstacles come her way.
nri_angle: Lamboria's CWG gold is part of India's dominant boxing performance in Glasgow, a point of pride for the Indian diaspora following the Games closely.
